title: Microprobe release ledger and rollout checklist
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick personal ledger for the next microprobe (small canary) release. This is a working checklist + rolling notes for the model flip on /v1/generate and the client-facing route /chat/production. Intended for 1–2 person execution, followed by handoff to oncall if we see instability.

Goals:
- Safely flip model variant from rwd-7b-v1 -> rwd-7b-v1-quant to shave token cost ~14% while keeping median p95 latency within SLOs.
- Validate quality on 12 golden prompts (see linked eval PR) and watch regression metrics.
- Avoid cross-tenant cold-start spikes; use staggered warmup by tenancy.

Quick notes / constraints:
- Target time window: 02:00–05:00 PT (low traffic)
- Max allowed error rate bump: +0.5% absolute on 5m error rate
- Latency soft threshold: p95 <= 420ms; hard cutoff 600ms (automated pinback)
- Token budget: initial burst 200k tokens across all cohorts
- Warmup approach: prefix caching + synthetic warm requests via warmup job (see commands)

Cohorts (microprobe sequencing):
1) Internal smoke (10 users) — feature-flagged via client-id list; sequence duration 5m
2) Beta tenants (3 tenants) — 2% traffic, duration 15m
3) Small public cohort (random 0.1% of traffic) — 60m (observability ramp)
4) Broad ramp to 5% if metrics stable for 60m

Checklist (pre-flip):
- [ ] Confirm canary image + model artifacts exist in registry and have SHA tag (registry: eu-west-1-redwood-dedicated)
- [ ] Validate quantized variant passes smoke runner locally (CLI: rwd serve local-smoke --model rwd-7b-v1-quant)
- [ ] Create canary rollout in console with exact pin config and fallback to rwd-7b-v1
- [ ] Add monitoring widgets for golden prompt drift (precision/recall where applicable)
- [ ] Schedule warmup job: warmup/warmup-runner --cohort beta --count 3000 --seed 42
- [ ] Notify oncall and CS slack channel #deploys ~30m before start

Checklist (during):
- [ ] Flip internal smoke cohort -> watch logs for OOM, GPU memory swap, and kv-cache misses (metric: kv_cache_miss_rate)
- [ ] Run BERT similarity check against golden prompts (script: scripts/eval/golden_similarity.sh)
- [ ] If error rate > +0.5% OR p95 > 420ms -> abort and pinback (command below)
- [ ] If quality regression on golden prompts > threshold -> abort and raise INF ticket
- [ ] After 60m of stable small public cohort -> raise to 5%

Rollback / pinback quick commands (operator cheats):
- Pinback via control plane: rwctl rollout pin --route /chat/production --model rwd-7b-v1 --reason "microprobe pinback"
- Immediate full rollback: rwctl rollout set-traffic --route /chat/production --fraction 0 --variant rwd-7b-v1
- Emergency isolate: rwctl isolate OR route-suppress --region us-west-2 --duration 30m

Telemetry to watch (dashboard rows):
- Per-route: p50/p95/p99 latency, request_rate, error_rate, backend_5xx
- Model-specific: kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_gpu_util, decode_tokens_per_sec, batch_size_avg
- Quality: golden_prompt_similarity_median, semantic_regression_count
- Cost: tokens_per_request, cost_estimated_per_minute (for the variant)

Acceptance heuristics (my quick rule-of-thumb):
- Stop immediately for sustained error rate > 0.5% absolute increase or p95 > 600ms for 5m
- Hold if golden prompt similarity drops by > 3% relative for 10m
- Allow ramp if all core metrics within soft thresholds for 60m and no quality regressions

Warmup and cache strategy notes:
- Warmup job should target cold clients first (client-header: X-Client-Id) to prime their KV caches
- Use deterministic prompts for prefix caching to maximize reuse, avoid hallucination-heavy prompts
- Avoid warmup for very long context (>1024) in first 15m to keep batched latency low

Observability and alerts I will arm before start:
- Slack alert: "deploy-microprobe-anya" with short summary and runbook link
- Pager rule: critical if p95 > 600ms for 3 consecutive 1m windows AND error rate > 1.0%
- Metric snapshot: capture pre-flip 15m baseline for p95/p50/error_rate/token_rate

Open questions / TODO for follow-up:
- Are there specific tenants that require manual opt-in due to compliance? (ask Harper)
- Confirm whether quantized variant uses the same KV cache format; if not, warmup semantics differ
- Validate fallback latency when routing triggers: is the fallback fast-path cold? (ticket INF-2150)

Post-release notes template (copy into final runbook):
- Time started: 
- Time stable/fully ramped: 
- Any observed regressions + artifacts (logs, traces): 
- Followups assigned: 

Hand-off one-liners for oncall if escalation: 
- "Pinned back to rwd-7b-v1 due to p95 breach at 03:12. Contact Anya/Diego for post-mortem."

Quick local commands I ran during testing (history snippet):
- rwctl dev start --model rwd-7b-v1-quant --cpu 4 --mem 32G
- scripts/eval/run_golden_batch.py --model rwd-7b-v1-quant --prompts data/golden/12.txt --out tmp/golden-results.json
- curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $LOCAL' -d @sample_payload.json https://local.redwood/v1/generate

Notes to self (stream of consciousness):
- Keep this doc minimal and copy to the shared deploy-runbook before go-time.
- If anything feels flakey during the internal smoke, stop and escalate rather than pushing deeper cohorts.
- Remember to run cost reconciliation with product after the ramp — quant gains may be offset by increased token churn if decoding changes.

End of ledger.
